title: Constitutional Classifiers for Code Generation Safety: Mitigating Jailbreaks in Codex-like Models
summary: This paper proposes adapting Constitutional Classifiers to enforce safety in code generation models like Codex. The approach trains classifiers on synthetic data generated via a constitution specifying safe coding practices. Evaluation on HumanEval and jailbreak prompts measures refusal rates, functional correctness, and memorization of unsafe code. The hypothesis is that this method reduces jailbreak success rates by 50% compared to baseline alignment techniques while maintaining 90% of Codex's original problem-solving accuracy.
gap: Existing alignment methods for code models (ref-001, ref-016) lack robust defenses against jailbreaks targeting code generation (ref-004, ref-014). Constitutional Classifiers (ref-004) have not been applied to code-specific safety domains.
approach: Train Constitutional Classifiers on synthetic code data generated by prompting LLMs with a constitution defining safe coding practices. Integrate classifiers as a guardrail during Codex inference, rejecting prompts that violate safety rules.
evaluation: Baselines: Vanilla Codex, RLHF-aligned Codex. Metrics: Jailbreak success rate (ref-014), HumanEval pass@k (ref-001), verbatim memorization of unsafe code (ref-007). Test on 100 jailbreak prompts and 200 HumanEval problems.
